sourceTasks: 3.2 Identify complementary or supplementary angles in polygons, including nonadjacent pairs.
3.3 Use straightedge and protractor to draw crossing lines, measure four angles, and discuss conjectures.
3.4 Work row-game angle measures and reconcile mismatched answers with a partner.
studentTask: Draw and measure all four angles of two original crossing lines; identify vertical pairs, justify a supplementary shared-angle argument, and compare results with another learner. Construct and label two separate angles 28° and 62° to explain complementarity without adjacency.

criteria.description: Draw two genuine intersecting straight lines and measure and label all four angles with a protractor.
Correctly identify two vertical-angle pairs and justify equal opposite measures using adjacent straight-angle sums.
Produce two separately constructed nonadjacent 28° and 62° angles and explain why their measures are complementary.
Compare measured figures or paired row-game solutions, find and explain an error, and revise the claim.

teacherRubric.passDecision: Teacher judgment only, based on actual student construction and reasoning.

cases.claim: Both opposite angles of 125° are equal; adjacent angles 55°; separate 28° and 62° sum to 90°.
cases.expected: Correct model, still requires human review of original student work.
Reject: those are adjacent supplementary angles, not a vertical pair.
Reject: they need only sum to 90°.

cases.claim: Numerical 125° supplied without a drawn, measured original intersection.
Bent lines or absent intersection labels.
cases.expected: Require a new valid construction; never auto-pass.
